messages:
alex: Heads-up — onboarding sample for the Workers/edge demo started failing after we changed the package exports in @redwood/sdk.
Error during `wrangler build`: "The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.js' does not provide an export named 'default'".

maria: ugh. do you have the package.json snippet? might be a conditional exports resolution issue in the bundler.

alex: pasted the relevant bits from the published package.json:
```json
{
  "main": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  },
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
}
```

sam: hmm that looks normal. many edge runtimes/bundlers ignore `module`/`main` and look only at `exports`. node's conditional exports are fine but some bundlers (wrangler/webpack in worker mode) pick the wrong subpath or don't support `types` resolution through the exports map. also TS sometimes can't find types if the bundler rewrites import to a subpath.

jon: saw a related CI failure: `TS2307: Cannot find module '@redwood/sdk' or its corresponding type declarations.` Repro: checkout `templates/edge-worker`, run `yarn && wrangler build`, fails reliably on node 18 image.

alex: quick manual repro: replace import with `import * as R from '@redwood/sdk'` — works locally with Node, fails in worker bundle. So it's an interoperability mismatch between Node resolve (which falls back to `module`/`main`) and the worker bundler (which strictly follows `exports` and expects additional subpaths).

maria: short-term fix: publish a patch that adds explicit fallback subpaths in `exports` and exposes types through the exports map. e.g. add:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
  },
  "./*": "./dist/*"
}
```
(not perfect but increases compatibility)

sam: also add a tiny CI job that runs the `templates/edge-worker` build on every release so we catch these regressions earlier. this is the place where SDK parity / packaging really shows up in onboarding.

pkg-bot: published @redwood/sdk@2.0.1-patch (fix/export-fallbacks) :package:

jon: opened PR with rollback + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/427 — includes a canary publish and a smoke test that runs `wrangler build` and checks for successful bundling.

alex: thanks. follow-ups: 1) add e2e sample build in release job, 2) add brief notes in the SDK changelog about exports map changes and edge compatibility, 3) create a tiny devex checklist for package.json export changes (who to ping, test matrix). :+1:

maria: agreed. I'll draft the checklist and add the CI job. tagging @sam for help with the wrangler pipeline.

sam: on it, will wire up the job and run it against the 2.0.1-patch canary later today.

alex: great — this one was painful for new users, want to make sure onboarding doesn't hit this again. :wave:
